Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. The formal statement gives $\alpha_2>0$, $|\alpha_1/\alpha_2+Y|\le CT^p\delta$, $\alpha_2\le|\mathbf a|\le(1+CT^p\delta)\alpha_2$, and $|\log(|\mathbf a|/a_{m ref})|\le\varepsilon$ at every $	au\in[0,T]$. It also supplies an invertible linear propagator from $k(	au_1)^\perp$ onto $k(	au_2)^\perp$ for $0\le	au_1\le	au_2\le T$, agreeing with every transverse amplitude solution and satisfying $\|\Phi\|\le252\exp(1)S|\mathbf a(	au_2)|/|\mathbf a(	au_1)|$ in the Euclidean operator norm. These retain all conclusions of Lemma 2.6 and specify its propagator constant. The generalization is from smooth $B$ on the physical interval to continuous $B$ on a compact set containing it. For a larger set, the four suprema defining $\delta$ are also taken over that set, so the smallness condition must still be checked there. The absolute factor $C$, integer exponent $p$ and integer threshold for $C_0$ are chosen before the wave data. The paper’s $CT^C$ notation is recovered by enlarging an absolute constant for $T\ge2$.
